facts.fact_text: In July 1994 Mr Stankov, as chairman of the Petrich branch of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden, requested the mayor of Petrich to authorise a meeting to be held on 31 July 1994 in the area of Samuilova krepost in commemoration of a historical event.
On 13 July 1994 the mayor of Petrich refused permission for the meeting requested by Mr Stankov, without giving any reasons.
The United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden appealed to the Petrich District Court against the mayor of Petrich's refusal of 13 July 1994.

Article 43 § 1 of the Bulgarian Constitution of July 1991 provides that everyone shall have the right to peaceful and unarmed assembly at meetings and marches.
Article 43 § 2 of the Bulgarian Constitution of July 1991 provides that the procedure for organising and holding meetings and marches shall be provided for by act of Parliament.
The legal requirements for the organisation of meetings are set out in the Bulgarian Meetings and Marches Act of 1990.

Section 12(2) of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990 provides that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council or the mayor shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it aims at the violent overturning of constitutional public order or is directed against the territorial integrity of the country, would endanger public order in the local community, or would breach the rights and freedoms of others.
Section 12(3) of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990 provides that the prohibition shall be imposed by a written reasoned act not later than twenty-four hours following the notification.

Section 12(4) of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990 provides that the organiser of the meeting, demonstration or march may appeal to the Executive Committee of the People's Council against the prohibition, and the Executive Committee shall decide within twenty-four hours.

The Government submitted that the allegation that the area of Samuilova krepost had been sealed off on 31 July 1994 was 'manifestly ill-founded'.

On 10 April 1995 the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden requested the mayor of Sandanski to authorise a meeting to be held on 22 April 1995 at the grave of Yane Sandanski at the Rozhen Monastery, on the occasion of the eightieth anniversary of his death.
On 14 April 1995 the mayor of Sandanski refused the request for a meeting on 22 April 1995, on the ground that the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden was not duly registered by the courts.

On 15 April 1995 the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden appealed to the Sandanski District Court against the mayor of Sandanski's refusal, stating inter alia that the Macedonian people had been deprived of their right to their own cultural life in violation of international law.
